batches_completed.source_doc: LORDS_OF_CIAN_Character_Codex_definitive.docx
batches_completed.note: Processed by a subagent given its size (~771KB), reviewed and merged by this session. This 'definitive' codex is internally messier than its filename suggests. (1) Biggest substantive conflict: the document repeatedly and consistently (in Kanja's, Pyro's, and Stormbreaker's own sections) states Pyro's mother was 'killed' during the Living Gate event and that Stormbreaker 'ended the vessel' — language that directly contradicts the ledger-locked fact that she is NOT dead but was fused into the Living Gate. This isn't a stray typo; it's the document's consistent internal framing, so it needs a human call on which version is canon. (2) The document gives two flatly incompatible identities for 'Lilith Cyzak' — a physical Karesian-adjacent 'Void-Dancer' bodyguard/anchor for Ozmund in one entry, and a desk-bound former Trust economic analyst with no physical power in a second, later entry (#31) — both claiming to be Ozmund's love interest/calibration point. (3) Structural oddities mirroring the kind you flagged before: the doc declares '─── END OF CHARACTER CODEX (26 entries) ───' partway through, then keeps going for nine more entries with an entry-numbering scheme ('#25–29,' then '#30,' '#31') that double-counts against the entries already included in the '26.' (4) The title page says 'v1.0' and a mid-document footer independently repeats 'v1.0,' yet the source file is named '...definitive.docx' — a version-label/filename mismatch worth flagging per your team's prior pattern of catching these. (5) Minor internal inconsistency: the Talisman of Mao's Stage 1 (Sovereign Umbrella) is said to protect '16 Avatars' in Kanja's own section, but Sephtis's, Anansi's, and Zora's sections all reference '17 Avatars' / Zora as the '17th crewmate.' (6) The opening ~130 lines of the document (before the first character header) begin mid-sentence and contain an entire block of battle-summary text duplicated verbatim back-to-back — almost certainly a copy-paste artifact from the docx export rather than intentional content, but worth a spot-check against the source file. On the positive side: every fact I checked against your existing locked ledger (Density Spike exclusivity, Kanja recovering rather than forging Onyx, the Crown-Scar being installed before the Verehimu ancestor's betrayal, Ezio/Valen as first cousins, the Triad Guardians originating from the Living Gate event, Anansi/Valeria as secret sisters, Archon Meridian as T.D.K.'s unknowing hidden son, and T.D.K.'s true name being Anu Un Ra with an explicit in-document note correcting an earlier 'Argul') was either confirmed outright or extended with compatible new detail — no other contradictions found.

rules.statement: No antithesis language. All capabilities are physical, engineered, or biological. The Ten Tongues system uses frequency, resonance, and density, described in physics terms only.
Mythic Realism. The narrative voice is Rorschach-Tolkien.
The Pi-Awakening occurs between Kanja's 314th and 315th birthday.
Kanja's Rebellion (ages 18-30) was against the Sovereign Trust (visible government), NOT the SBD. The SBD is clandestine, uncovered in the Book 1 epilogue.

Institutional naming: the Sovereign Trust is the visible government. The Directorate is the informal name for the Trust's enforcement apparatus, used in common speech, especially labor districts and rebellion-era records. The SBD is the clandestine layer beneath both. Three names, one institutional architecture.
Hermes is now Fermand Aurelias. Hermes remains as an operational alias only.
Varro Kharas is now Lord Varro Dominael, "The Crownless Marshal."
Archon Thorne is discarded. Does not exist.
Archon Meridian is Archon Un Ra, T.D.K.'s hidden son. He does not know this.
Varkul's morphing is a natural adaptive response to habitat, not a transformation power. Land Form and Hydro-Titan Form are both canon. The Harrow Ring is hydrodynamic physics.
Lady Nadea Thren is an independent operator who defected FROM the SBD. She is NOT T.D.K.'s champion and NOT "Glass Ordained." She is Ezio's patron. The Mirrored Chorus dissolved upon her departure.

Pyro's hidden birth name is Ignis. "Pyro" is a ship-name. Her birth is NATURAL. The Dhar-Kael bond was completed by her mother (the last keeper) BEFORE T.D.K.'s Living Gate curse. The Demaron event is separate from and after the birth; Stormbreaker's trauma is preserved, resequenced rather than replaced.
Onyx is Kanja's Blade. SBD blackscribe origin. Black Ledger chronicler. Sentient Drakma Longsword, royal Karesian.

Ozmund's Density Spike is Karesian inheritance, active from birth with an early trigger at age 2. He carries the Crown-Scar plus Kares Prime Kareth War-Order blood, meaning T.D.K.'s command architecture running on Karesian hardware. He has full conscious density control without an Awakening.

Ozmund's Book 1 arc: his father Aethelgard Verehimu and Kanja's father Maro Rexmar are both murdered at the Fulfillment Ceremony (Book 1's opening) -> he rejects the crown -> hires Ezio to investigate -> enters Maw circuits -> discovers the Crown-Scar truth (T.D.K.'s neural architecture in every Verehimu) -> takes the Venim surname, shedding Verehimu -> builds the Unchained Legion -> Red Beard brings 150,000 Cestari -> defects to the Shattered Kingdoms at the climax -> marches on T.D.K.
Project Apotheosis and Subject 0-Alpha are LIVE THREATS discovered during the Book 1 investigation, not resolved backstory.
Lauris Letitia's Anomalous Mass is density without corresponding weight, Karesian biology from Kares Prime. She doesn't sink because her density has no weight; the physics cannot reconcile the two.
Lauris is full-blooded Karesian. NOT a lab product, NOT manufactured, NOT a Lattice-Amplification Variant.
Lauris is a former SBD contractor who left voluntarily. Ezio offered clarity; she accepted.
Lauris's weapons: Aristocrat (rapier), Spine of Dagon (6.2ft greatsword with Swallow sheath), Attia's Rite (Kanja-forged breaker), Phalanx (Night-Glass / Solar-Spire / Phoenix-Guard / Triad-Lock).

Lauris Letitia is the last born pure-blood Karesian before the men died and the women ruled alone. The pinnacle of Karesian biology, surpassing all pure-bloods before her, and the biological ceiling of an extinct cooperation between Karesian men and women. She will inherit two battle artifacts from the Kareth sisters (details deferred to "Session Lock 2, April 11 2026" -- not yet located in this corpus).
rules.note: Full backstory/psych profile/capability profile deferred to a document not yet found: 'Session Lock 2 (April 11, 2026)'.

rules.statement: The Dhar-Kael (the Bound Ones) are a clade of three companion species bonded symbiotically with Karesian biology: Tide-Back Coursers (Varkul's species, land/water), Oath-Raptors (Varruk's species, sky), Apex-Felines (Sorya's species, shadow/memory). Imprint happens during a juvenile window. The bond is permanent, biological, non-transferable. Pyro's mother was the last keeper of the tradition. Three survivors remain; when they die, the clade is extinct.

The Vael Kem (the Hollow Tide) are a deep-ocean civilization with pressure-based biology, the inverse of Karesian density. They consumed Dhar-Kael as a food source and drove them to near-extinction. The Rexmar bloodline's military tradition was forged in this war, protecting what cannot protect itself. The Vael Kem are scattered, not destroyed.

T.D.K. (Anu Un Ra) military structure: Division 1 Weights/Conquest, Champion General Baryon, open warfare. Division 2 Echoes/Nameless Pursuit, Champion Sereth Vaul "The Silencer," tracking/pursuit/Ever-Haunt. Division 3 Mirages/Illusions, Champion Lady Vestige, illusion warfare. Division 4 Crownless Host/Dominion, Champion Lord Varro Dominael, undead legions/siege. Division 5, post-Thren replacement Champion Bolo Troth, function TBD. The Mirrored Chorus dissolved upon Nadea Thren's defection. 5 active champions, 5 active divisions.

The Era Zero War is REMOVED from canon. Project Apotheosis and Subject 0-Alpha are now active threats discovered during Book 1's investigation, not resolved backstory. Ozmund's entire military arc (crown rejection, Venim identity, Unchained Legion, Red Beard's 150,000-Cestari defection) occurs within Book 1's present narrative.

Crown-Scar mechanics: a neural residue graft of T.D.K.'s command-frequency architecture, bioelectrically integrated, designed to be hereditary. The root-access tether was lost when Haku's campaigns fractured T.D.K.'s infrastructure. It was given BEFORE Verehimu's betrayal; T.D.K. created his own downfall tool.

Archon Un Ra is T.D.K.'s hidden son, placed under the name "Meridian." He does not know his parentage. His role expands post-Epilogue. He is the direct Un Ra bloodline, not a Crown-Scar bearer: Archon's true name is Archon Un Ra, and his claim to T.D.K.'s lineage runs through birth, not through the Crown-Scar installation mechanism used on the Verehimu line.
rules.note: Resolves OPEN-003. Ruled by Abad 2026-08-22: 'Archon is THE direct descendent of Anu Un Ra. Archon's true name is Archon Un Ra.'

rules.statement: The Talisman of Mao has 3 stages, 9 substages total. Stage 1, Sovereign Umbrella, recipient the Crew: sub1 Shadow-Pulse (lattice-awareness + digital invisibility), sub2 Blight Immunity (frequency neutralization), sub3 Kinetic Buffer (Newtonian dampening). Stage 2, Grounded Bastion, recipient the Planet: sub1 Heavy Hand (density transfer through contact), sub2 Foundry Anvil (radiance channeled into subterranean strata), sub3 Gravity-Fetter pendant AND Architectural Reinforcement / Lattice-Coupling, blended as one mechanic (see MCD-061). Stage 3, Internal Quench, recipient the Captain: sub1 Bone-Tempering, sub2 Biological Total-Lock, sub3 Governor's Shackle.

Resolution of CONFLICT-001 (Grounded Bastion Substage 3): the Gravity-Fetter pendant and Architectural Reinforcement/Lattice-Coupling are cause and effect within it, per Abad's direct ruling (2026-08-13). This resolves the lighthouse/Pi-Awakening staging.

Book 1, "The Deposed King." Opening: murder scene, two kings dead, Ezio and Fermand investigate, hired by Ozmund. Three acts: Investigation -> 10-Day Interregnum -> Karkosa Heist. Epilogue: the Great Breach, SBD uncovered, T.D.K.'s 5,000-year dormancy ends.

Maw system terms: Maw (the venue/sport/institution), Grand Maw (mega-venues), the Slab (combat floor), Branded (any fighter in the Maw system), Branded Peak, Proven, Shaper, Shapers' Compact, Blood Writ, Proving, Brand-Line, the Display.
Maw House System, four tiers: Pillars (7 founding Houses), Banners (30-40 Great Houses), Standards (300-500 chartered Houses), Pits (thousands, unlicensed).
Grand Circuit progression: Pit Circuits -> Regional Circuits -> Provincial Provings -> Grand Circuit -> the Apex (Karkosa, annual) -> the Reclamation (Vakas, every 50 years).

Vakas, the Reclamation, is not a death match, it is a judgment. Scales to ~150% of the champion's density. Evaluates authenticity, courage, innovation, integrity. Approved fighters unlock the Proven tier (5,000-8,000x). Corrupt or fraudulent champions die.

Red Beard: Reclamation-Proven at 7,000x. Trained with Ozmund in secret. Current density 16,000x actual, ceiling approximately 18,000x. The world believes he is 4,800x. Parents: Handler-4412 and Handler-6019. The Quiet Table fed 3,000 Cestari across twelve Maws for nine years. Executed on the Slab of Maw-7.

Kanja's surrender was political, not military. King Maro Rexmar and Aethelgard Verehimu secretly negotiated a pact; when both are murdered at the Fulfillment Ceremony, the pact dies. The Book 1 investigation is about who killed a peace.

Lineage locks: Maro Rexmar is Kanja's father. Drakmund Verehimu is the Evil King, Aethelgard's father, exiled by Aethelgard, alive in the Shattered Kingdoms, capable, carrying a Crown-Scar. Aethelgard Verehimu was king for one month before the double regicide.

The Double Regicide: both Maro Rexmar and Aethelgard Verehimu are murdered at the Fulfillment Ceremony, killed by the Three Ronin with SBD wet-work support team cover-up. The Fulfillment Ceremony is separate from the Sovereign Pier Accords, roughly 296 years apart.
rules.note: A-3 (Abad, 2026-08-23) confirms this rule already states the resolution the audit asked for; no change needed.

rules.statement: The Three Ronin: the Silence (Decimus Korr, 2,800x), the Ghost (unknown name, Lawless Reaches, 180x), the Blade (Serai Noth, 3,400x). An SBD wet-work team of 6-8 sanitizes after each operation. Reckonings: Silence by Red Beard (Book 4), Ghost by Anansi/Valeria (Book 4), Blade by Valen (Book 5).

The Beloved (Ronin victims, Book 3): Nelle Adessi, healer, 38x, killed mid-ledger-entry. Tomas Grieve, builder, 220x, killed reaching for the door to help Nelle. A coordinated 94-second Ronin operation, all three Ronin involved.

Shattered Kingdoms geography: world split roughly Shattered Kingdoms 75%, Sovereign Trust 15%, Jicome 10%. Five nations: Aethel-Gard (neutral), Obsidian Prefecture (antagonist), Astral Archipelago (allied), Celestial Zenith (allied through Orlok), Hollow Shogunate (antagonist, Book 3+). The Kingdoms of Merak are a pre-Old Dominion civilization T.D.K. purged over roughly 30,000-40,000 years.
Archipelago characters: Soledad Keme is the true name of the Singularity (First Seat). Toussaint Louverture is the true name of the Event Horizon / Master Void-Cusp, the Singularity's Champion.

Orlok finalized: age 76,003 years. Density variable, resting 12,000x, combat 16,000-18,000x, ascension 20,000x with a reforged staff. Four disciplines only: Density Manipulation, Kinetic Ascension, Density Sight, the Vault. Enlightenment is triggered by the Vakas draw (Book 4).

Book 3, The Dark Monarch: Crown-Scar arc, Shogunate war, Archon as a third force. Book 4, The Broken Meridian: alliance converges, Orlok vs Vakas (the draw). Book 5, The Miner's Son: three fronts, T.D.K. contained, Pyro peaks, Orlok transcends.
Book 5 Gate Battle: Orlok holds the Broken Meridian entrance. Gate team: Orlok, Anansi, Ezio, Fermand, Toussaint Louverture. Ezio's cover dies at the gate; the gate lives.

Post-Book-5: T.D.K. is contained, not killed. Ever-Haunt is freed from direction. The Shattered Kingdoms are left unresolved. Drakmund Verehimu is alive as an open thread. Archon Meridian is an unresolved third force.
The Dark Monarch (Book 3): the Crown-Scar is a CHOICE Ozmund makes. "The Dark Monarch" is a title the world gives him. Kanja does NOT lose in this series. Red Beard delivers the awakening.

Val Saeryn Kareth is Kanja's mother. Val Mirel Kareth is Ozmund's mother. They are sisters, both Karesian. Kanja and Ozmund are cousins through their mothers, not their fathers. Ages: Val Saeryn 93,179 years, Val Mirel 89,003 years.

rules.statement: Jicome is Haku's unified kingdom: a Rex mainland (capital Rexhaven) and a Mar archipelago, united by Haku and held by the Rexmar line after him. The Sovereign Trust Domain (capital Karkosa, including Stormshelter Cove and Maw-7 Slab) is a SEPARATE, distinct territory, not Jicome under another name. ORIGINAL TEXT, SUPERSEDED: "Jicome is the mapped Sovereign Trust Domain..."

The Regional Atlas's 'Jicome' region (capital Rexhaven, far northwest) IS the Rex/mainland half of the nation of Jicome (see corrected MCD-110). ORIGINAL TEXT, SUPERSEDED: "The Atlas's separate 'Jicome' region... is not the nation of Jicome..."
FLAGGED, not resolved: whether 'Southern Seaboard' means Jicome's coastline, the Sovereign Trust Domain's coastline, or both. Needs Abad's direct ruling before Phase 1 item 5 proceeds.

The Haku unification: Jicome holds a mainland (Rex bloodline) and its own archipelago (Mar bloodline), both descending from the same Rex/Mar stock. Haku united the two into one people and one kingdom.

After Haku, the Rexmar line held Jicome as functional Kings of the Sea, then five successive generations traded functional power for ceremonial Royalty: Turey, Amaru, Yabura, Yaro, Maro Rexmar (Kanja's father, assassinated at the Sovereignty Summit).
The Meridian Compact and the Sovereign Trust are NOT the same institution. The Meridian Compact is its own distinct faction, led by Archon Meridian (Archon Un Ra, T.D.K.'s hidden son).

The naming link is deliberate: Archon Meridian leads the Meridian Compact, and the name is his father's. Archon Meridian is Archon Un Ra, T.D.K.'s hidden son, placed under that name by his father, unaware of his true parentage. The name 'Meridian' traces to Anu Un Ra's ancient identity as 'the Ash-King of Broken Meridian.'

Four Pillars govern every sentence: Pillar 1 Rorschach-Tolkien Voice, Pillar 2 Zafonian Gothic Noir, Pillar 3 Modern Laconic Spartan, Pillar 4 Mythic Realism. Governs tone/language only, does not assert story facts.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: Pillar 1, Rorschach-Tolkien Voice: layering, not compromise. Rorschach layer drops articles and pronouns, staccato rhythm. Tolkien layer uses Germanic-root diction (sunder not break, hew not cut, offal not trash, delve not dig, carrion not garbage), never modern slang.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: Pillar 2, Zafonian Gothic Noir: settings are alive and malevolent, the environment is a character, weather is mood, architecture is psychological. Sensory priority is smell/touch/sound before naming the emotion.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: Pillar 3, Modern Laconic Spartan (all dialogue): the 50% rule, draft dialogue naturally then cut at least half the words. No phatic communication. Fact over emotion. Permitted humor is irony and understatement only.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: Pillar 4, Mythic Realism: if it cannot be described in terms of mass, sound, pressure, or chemistry, it does not exist. Karesian Prose Rule: descriptions of Karesian/high-density characters must imply mass and momentum as atmospheric distortion from density, not special effects.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: No antithesis: never balance clauses. Use cumulative evidence piling instead. No antithesis language: the words magic, sorcery, supernatural, mystical, deity, god, goddess do not exist in this world; all capabilities are physical, engineered, biological, or procedural. Consistent with MCD-001.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: The Density Spike is never named in prose. 'Spike' is a codex term only. In narrative the reader experiences the effect only.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: Violence is physics: every combat description is written in terms of mass, velocity, force, structural failure, and biological consequence, never abstract power. Powers through sensation, never delivered as a textbook explanation.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: No borrowed terminology, absolute replacements: Colosseum to Maw, Gladiator to Branded, Lanista to Shaper, Bookmaker to Reckoner, Arena to Maw/Slab. Show-don't-tell protocol.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: Five designated narrators, one per narrative thread: Onyx of Oblivion (Kanja chapters), Red Beard (Ozmund chapters), Ezio Valcari (investigation chapters), Fermand Aurelias (investigation chapters, alternate), Anansi (scattered POV chapters, infrequent).
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: Narrator 1, Onyx of Oblivion: Moral absolutism, Iron (true/heavy) or Rust (false/hollow), never grey area. Maxim: 'Mercy is earned. Memory is the receipt.' Never names the Density Spike.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: Narrator 2, Red Beard: observes/assesses/reports without editorializing. Always addresses Ozmund as 'General,' never 'Oz' or his first name. Never speaks to enemies he intends to kill.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: Narrator 3, Ezio Valcari: Zafon Gothic/Noir atmosphere fused with Twain-Marx wit. Never breaks character to explain the investigation to the reader.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: Narrator 4, Fermand Aurelias: clinical/methodical, no slang, no contractions, no panic ever. Only 'My dear Ezio' receives warmth.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: Narrator 5, Anansi: scattered POV chapters, infrequent. Voice fragments across multiple perspectives.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: Character dialogue voices, each meant to be attributable without a speaker tag: Kanja, Ozmund, Valen, Sephtis, Orlok, Lilith, Valeria, Damu, Matar, Cooper each with distinct diction.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: Every POV sequence follows a four-step cadence: environmental read, threat assessment, verdict, action.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx

rules.statement: Exclusion list, if any of these appear in a draft the draft is wrong. Banned words: magic, sorcery, supernatural, mystical, deity, god, goddess, divine, enchanted, spell, mana, arcane, conjure, bewitch, hex, incantation, ritual (in a mystical context). Banned terminology: Colosseum, gladiator, gladiatorial, lanista, arena (as venue), bookmaker, Valkyrie, leaf-blade, gate-born, Era Zero. Banned structures: balanced antithesis clauses, 'not only X but also Y,' 'while X is true, Y is also true.' Banned narration: characters explaining their powers to the reader, textbook ability descriptions, info-dumps. Banned dialogue: phatic communication, characters explaining the plot to each other, villains monologuing plans.
rules.source: Voice_Bible_Definitive.docx
rules.note: The banned term 'Era Zero' here is consistent with MCD-051.

rules.source: Arsenal_of_Cian_Definitive_Edition_v2

rules.statement: The Moonvault is a hidden ~2,000-person smith settlement, led by Haryn Dael, using caldera-native Ore-Oxen.
rules.source: Arsenal_of_Cian_Definitive_Edition_v2

rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: Every fifty years Vargo Vakas returns to test the reigning Apex Champion. Four outcomes: Survival with Honor, Survival with Silence, Death, the Exception.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: Competitive tiers run: Pit Circuits -> Regional Circuits -> Provincial Provings -> the Grand Circuit -> the Apex.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: The Seven Pillar Houses: Dravos, Korrath, Velthari, Maekar, Osseren, Threnn, Selenar, each with a founding-era doctrine and patron dynasty.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: Historical head-to-head win rates between Pillar doctrines, used by Reckoners for odds-setting.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: Sable Kin (House Osseren) exposed a Shaper's bout-rigging scheme ~400 years ago; the only Pillar demotion in Maw history.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: Valor Thenn (House Threnn) holds the highest Proven elevation in Maw history: 8,000x, 'Upper Proven.'
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: The Iron Veil (House Velthari) retired 188-0, the only Apex Champion to trigger Vakas's Exception and survive it.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: House Vennrik lost its patron and became available; Ozmund enters under 'Venim.' CONFLICT-CHECK: document frames this as 'Book 1'; MCD-100 controls (Book 3).
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: House Galthorn ('the Black Ledger') is the Maw's open secret, an untraceable Banner whose patron has never been identified.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: House Draeven ('the Second Sons') exclusively recruits non-inheriting noble sons and daughters.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: House Brekka ('the Breaker's Yard') is patronized by the Keldane Settlement Cooperative, built into Stormshelter Cove infrastructure.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: House Sektori, House Durnwall, House Aravel, House Rathaan, House Morvane, House Tolvari, each with distinct doctrines and flagship fighters.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: Pillars hold permanent hereditary Council seats; Banners hold state-issued renewable charters.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: The Pits are unlicensed combat operations in four escalating tiers: Basement, Circuit, Named, Blood Pits.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: Named Pits: the Crucible Market, the Keldane Hollow, the Black Slab, the Ember Circuit.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: A Shaper is state-licensed via the Blood Writ. The Shapers' Compact is led by the seven-seat Iron Council.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: Kael Threnn is Ozmund's Shaper. Harren Bladesmith, the Ghost Surgeon, Maja Stormseed, Seraph Keld, Derra Thenn, Oren Drask are other named Shapers.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: The Grand Maw of Karkosa, 'the Throat,' is the Maw system's symbolic and operational center, 120,000 capacity.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: Named Regional Grand Maws: Maw-1 'The Mother,' Maw-7 'the Keldane Maw'/'Slab of Judgment,' Maw-12 'the Teeth,' Maw-3 'the Belly,' Maw-15 'the Drowning Floor,' the Ash Maw/'the Scar.'
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: Standard licensed-Maw Slab construction is Dead Drakma composite over basalt bedrock. Seating organized in a strict social hierarchy.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: Cestari are bred at ~40 licensed 'Farms' via density-optimization pairing.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: A Cestari brand is applied within 72 hours of birth. Handlers operate in four tiers.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: The Brand-Line operates through four coded methods: Scarification Coding, Wall Inscription, Ritual Encoding, Transport Relay.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: Cestari manumission requires cumulative Scrip value to exceed maintenance cost by a fixed 3:1 ratio.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: The Marker Rebellion, the Long Walk, and Kanja's Long Mask-era liberations are the largest resistance operations in Maw history.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: The Maw economy's seven revenue streams: Betting (~40%), Sponsorship/Patronage, Gate Access, Fighter Transfers, Merchandising, Scrip-Transaction Value, State Taxation.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: A Reckoner is a state-chartered betting professional. Odds are set via a three-factor model.
rules.source: Maw_Codex_Definitive_Edition.docx

rules.statement: The Osseren Starvation Ring, the Dead Pool, and the Tether Arbitrage are the Maw's three major historical scandals.

rules.statement: Aethel-Gard is highland plateau, fjord, and sub-arctic tundra, ruled by a Dual Court. The Verehimu bloodline originates here. Alignment: neutral.
rules.source: Shattered_Kingdoms_Political_Atlas

rules.statement: The Obsidian Prefecture is a western inland plateau power, ruled by a Senate of twelve Patriarchs. Alignment: antagonist.
rules.source: Shattered_Kingdoms_Political_Atlas

rules.source: Shattered_Kingdoms_Political_Atlas

rules.source: Shattered_Kingdoms_Political_Atlas

rules.statement: The Hollow Shogunate is an eastern volcanic archipelago, ruled by Vile-Sire and Hollow-Dam through Parasitic Sovereignty. Alignment: antagonist, Book 3+.

T.D.K. conditioned and kenneled specimens using Ionic Rite methodology; the kennels collapsed in the Great Breach (Book 1 epilogue), releasing them under Sereth Vaul's field command.
rules.source: World Codex v3.4, Section 5.5 (full subsection)

Anu preserved critical infrastructure while letting the visible empire collapse, then rebuilt in the Shattered Kingdoms' hidden coastal corner.
rules.source: World Codex v3.4, Section 6.7

rules.source: World Codex v3.4, Section VII

rules.statement: Five-book series structure: Book 1 The Deposed King (murder investigation -> 10-Day Interregnum -> Pi-Awakening -> Great Breach epilogue), Book 2 The Ever-Haunt, Book 3 The Dark Monarch (Ozmund vs T.D.K., Crown-Scar revelation escalates), Book 4 The Broken Meridian (alliance converges, Orlok vs Vakas the draw), Book 5 The Miner's Son (three fronts, T.D.K. contained, Pyro peaks, Orlok transcends).
rules.source: World Codex v3.4, Sections XIII-XIV
rules.note: Promoted to locked with Book 4/5 titles corrected in place: this rule's original text still carried '(TBD)' placeholders for Book 4 and Book 5, superseded by the already-locked MCD-097's real titles. Book 1 ('The Deposed King') and Book 2 ('The Ever-Haunt') titles are this rule's own contribution -- no other locked rule states them. Resolved during the Batch 45 draft-reconciliation pass, per Abad's authorization: "you have my authorization to reconcile".

rules.statement: Kanja's Twenty-Two Victories (ages 18-30) are individually named and classified: 16 conventional/labor-logistics victories plus 6 classified as 'Unwinnable' by the Directorate (each earning Kanja a new alias): The Storm That Walks, The Lord of Embers, The Iron Bastard's Stand, The Night of the Crow King, The Siege of the Ghost Harbor, The Battle of the Black Trench (Bane).
rules.source: World Codex v3.4, Sections XVI-XVII
rules.note: Superseded by MCD-230 (Batch 41), which corrects the imprecise '16 conventional' paraphrase with the source document's own precise 10+6+6 breakdown.

rules.statement: Density Tiers 0 through 6 with named exemplars: Tier 0 Baseline 25x (average Jicome civilian), Tier 1 Elite 100-500x (Cassius Verehimu 100x), Tier 2 Military 500-1,000x (Colonel Draconis 700x), Tier 3 Branded Peak 2,200-4,900x (Red Beard public 4,800x), Tier 3.5 Reclamation-Proven 5,000-8,000x (fewer than 200 in history, Red Beard's actual concealed density is 16,000x), Tier 4 Synthetic Apex 20,000x (Vargo Vakas Prime), Tier 5 Density Spike (Kanja/Ozmund, variable/limitless), Tier 6 Sovereign Mass classified (Anu Un Ra/T.D.K., heavier than Vargo Vakas).
rules.source: World Codex v3.4, Section XII

rules.statement: Pyro's mother is NOT dead. When the Demaron entity took hold of her, T.D.K.'s Living Gate (voice-keyed breach-lattice) was deployed as a containment mechanism, designed to seal the threat away. She inverted the Gate's function into a forge instead of letting it seal her along with the entity. That act transformed her rather than ending her: she is fused into the Gate's own architecture, no longer flesh in the ordinary sense, bound into the boundary she built. The Triad Guardians (Varkul, Varruk, Sorya) are what she pushed outward through that inversion before the fusion completed, permanently bonded to Pyro.
rules.source: Operator ruling, 2026-08-22: 'i love that angle. apporved'
rules.note: Resolves OPEN-006. Supersedes the SBD Directives' 'termination... with Kanja's consent' account as the operative truth -- that account stands per CONFLICT-002 as the Directorate's own cold institutional read of watching a person stop being flesh and start being infrastructure, not a lie exactly, but not what actually happened either. Does not contradict MCD-022 (birth natural, Demaron event separate from birth, no prior mention of the mother being terminated) -- this rule gives that separate event a concrete physical outcome instead of leaving it undefined.

rules.statement: Pyro's birth and his mother's transformation into the Living Gate are two effects of the same single event -- described as Pyro being 'born in the severed instant' -- not two separate events with a gap between them. This narrows MCD-022's 'separate from and after the birth' framing to mean sequentially distinct within the same event, not separated by meaningful time.
rules.source: Operator ruling, 2026-08-22, resolving the WC-017/MCD-022 sequencing note flagged during Batch 9 review
rules.note: A future book-level scene can still play the transformation and the birth as distinct beats within one continuous sequence -- this rule fixes only that they are not separated by an extended interval, since the Directorate's own account (already ruled unreliable) implied a longer institutional process.

rules.statement: Kanja's full name is Kanja Haku Rexmar; "Haku" is a middle name taken from the ancestor who defeated T.D.K.
rules.source: Character Codex, Kanja Rexmar — Canon Mandates

rules.statement: Kanja's Density Spike ability is post-Awakening only and is exclusive to the Rexmar and Verehimu bloodlines.
rules.source: Character Codex, Kanja Rexmar — Canon Mandates
rules.note: Consistent with locked fact (Density Spike exclusive to Kanja and Ozmund); adds the "post-Awakening only" qualifier as new detail, not a contradiction.

rules.statement: Kanja recovered Onyx of Oblivion; he did not forge it, and it pre-dates his smithing career by millennia.
rules.source: Character Codex, Onyx of Oblivion — Canon Mandates
rules.note: Reinforces locked fact that Kanja recovered rather than forged Onyx.

rules.statement: Kanja and Ozmund are cousins through their mothers, who were Kareth War-Order war-sisters (Val Saeryn Kareth and Val Mirel Kareth).
rules.source: Character Codex, Kanja Rexmar — Key Relationships; Ozmund Verehimu — Key Relationships

rules.statement: Kanja's Long Mask persona lasted 284 years, ending when the Gravity-Fetter pendant was severed at the Gilded Lighthouse, triggering the Pi-Awakening.
rules.source: Character Codex, Kanja Rexmar — Canon Mandates

rules.statement: Kanja's Pi-Awakening occurs between his 314th and 315th birthday ("Day 0" = age 314).
rules.source: Character Codex, Kanja Rexmar — Canon Mandates
rules.note: Consistent with locked fact that Pi-Awakening occurs at 314.

rules.statement: The Gravity-Fetter pendant is the physical interface for the Talisman of Mao's "Governor's Shackle" function, not a separate object; severing it destabilizes the Shackle and triggers Pi-Awakening completion.
rules.source: Character Codex, Kanja Rexmar — Canon Lock (explicit in-document canon lock statement)

rules.statement: Kanja fought 22 documented battles between ages 18 and 30 (10 conventional victories, 6 infrastructure/labor victories, 6 classified 'Unwinnable' victories) before surrendering the Trinity to his father, King Maro Rexmar.
rules.source: Character Codex, Kanja Rexmar — The Ten Victories / Unwinnable Victories

rules.statement: King Maro Rexmar negotiated the secret Sovereign Pier Accords with Aethelgard Verehimu, promising Directorate recognition of Maro as sovereign King of Jicome in exchange for Kanja surrendering the Trinity; the pact died when Aethelgard was murdered at the Sovereignty Summit (Book 1 opening).
rules.source: Character Codex, Kanja Rexmar — Battle 10 (The Sovereign Pier)

rules.statement: Kanja's SBD designation is SBD-001.
rules.source: Character Codex, Pyro — Biological Standard

rules.statement: Onyx of Oblivion is a sentient Drakma longsword (Living Blade/Heuristic Engine), not a person, and is the primary Third Person Limited narrator for all Kanja POV chapters.
rules.source: Character Codex, Onyx of Oblivion — What Onyx Is / Canon Mandates

rules.statement: Onyx was sealed in the Directorate Vaults (L9, "the Silent Infinite") for the entire 284-year Long Mask period.
rules.source: Character Codex, Onyx of Oblivion — The 284-Year Abandonment

rules.statement: Onyx's Black Ledger is Drakma lattice-memory — a permanent, un-redactable record of everything the blade witnesses.
rules.source: Character Codex, Onyx of Oblivion — The Black Ledger

rules.statement: Ozmund Verehimu's birth name is Ozmund Verehimu; he adopts the surname Venim during Book 1 after rejecting the throne.
rules.source: Character Codex, Ozmund Verehimu — Identity / Canon Mandates

rules.statement: Ozmund is 203 years old and his Density Spike activated at age 2, two years ahead of the standard trigger age.
rules.source: Character Codex, Ozmund Verehimu — Identity / Background

rules.statement: Ozmund's bloodline is Verehimu (paternal) plus Kareth War-Matriarchy (maternal, via Val Mirel Kareth).
rules.source: Character Codex, Ozmund Verehimu — Identity

rules.statement: Unlike Kanja, Ozmund has full conscious control of his Density Spike without requiring an Awakening.
rules.source: Character Codex, Ozmund Verehimu — The Gravity Specialist

rules.statement: The Crown-Scar is a hereditary neural residue graft of T.D.K.'s (Anu Un Ra's) command architecture, engineered into the first Verehimu BEFORE the ancestor's betrayal of T.D.K., as a succession tool.
rules.source: Character Codex, Ozmund Verehimu — Background; Anu Un Ra — The Crown-Scar
rules.note: Confirms/reinforces the locked correction that the Crown-Scar was installed before the betrayal, not during or after.

rules.statement: The Crown-Scar's root-access tether to T.D.K. was severed during Haku's (Kanja's ancestor's) campaigns; if the tether is ever re-established, every living Verehimu (including Ozmund) becomes T.D.K.'s asset.
rules.source: Character Codex, Ozmund Verehimu — Canon Mandates; Anu Un Ra — The Crown-Scar

rules.statement: Red Beard, not Ozmund, narrates all Ozmund POV chapters; the two are explicitly stated to be separate individuals frequently conflated in-world.
rules.source: Character Codex, Red Beard — Identity / Canon Mandates

rules.statement: Red Beard's true name is Tarn Cestari; "Cestari" is a slave-caste brand, not a surname, and he was born property in the Old Dominion's Maw gladiatorial economy.
rules.source: Character Codex, Red Beard — Identity / Origin

rules.statement: Red Beard's publicly known density is 4,800x (upper Branded Peak); his actual concealed density is 16,000x and climbing, known only to have been trained with Ozmund in secret.
rules.source: Character Codex, Red Beard — Identity

rules.statement: Red Beard defected to Ozmund's Unchained Legion during Book 1, bringing roughly 150,000 freed Cestari fighters and their families.
rules.source: Character Codex, Red Beard — The Defection

rules.statement: Lilith Cyzak is Ozmund's love interest and "calibration point"; per Ozmund's own Canon Mandates, "Valeria is Kanja's — Lilith is Ozmund's."
rules.source: Character Codex, Ozmund Verehimu — Canon Mandates
rules.note: Consistent with MCD-134's fuller profile.

rules.statement: The document contains two mutually incompatible profiles for a character named Lilith Cyzak: one as a physical 'Void-Dancer' of House Verehimu who grounds Ozmund's density by touch (Ghost-Step Algorithm, Thread-Relay + Base-Grout abilities, no economic background stated), and a separate, later entry (#31) as a former Sovereign Trust economic analyst with no physical density-related power who decodes Directorate communications and calibrates Ozmund through cost-benefit reasoning.
rules.source: Character Codex, Lilith Cyzak (first entry) vs Lilith Cyzak (CC Entry #31)
rules.note: RESOLVED per MCD-134 (2026-08-22): the economic-analyst profile (Codex entry #31) is the base canon builds from, now substantially expanded (Ozmund's-blood transfusion durability, combat training arc, economic-terrorism capability). The 'Void-Dancer' profile in this entry is discarded and is not canon in any form.

rules.statement: Ezio Valcari and Valen (Sinisterblade) are first cousins of House Valcari, sharing the 'Sinister Bloodline' martial tradition.
rules.source: Character Codex, Ezio Valcari — The Sinister Bloodline; Valen — The Sinister Bloodline
rules.note: Confirms the locked fact that Ezio and Valen/Sinisterblade are first cousins.

rules.statement: Ezio Valcari is publicly known as a theorist/spymaster, but is classified as an elite close-quarters combatant capable of killing a room in three seconds; this is known only to Valen, Sephtis, Kanja, Anansi, and Lauris.
rules.source: Character Codex, Ezio Valcari — Identity / Canon Mandates
rules.note: Amended in Batch 44 to add Lauris per Abad's explicit ruling ('she does know') resolving a conflict raised by the Psychological Profiles document, which states she has seen the Valcari War-Side in action and that her Attia role includes deliberate cover-maintenance for Ezio (see CC-111).

rules.statement: Ezio Valcari is 75 years old with 750 years of wisdom-equivalence gained through training under Sephtis.
rules.source: Character Codex, Ezio Valcari — Identity

rules.statement: Ezio's patron is Lady Nadea Thren, a defected SBD analyst operating independently.
rules.source: Character Codex, Ezio Valcari — Identity

rules.statement: The movement's 'revolutionary trio' is Ezio Valcari (the Architect/strategy), Fermand/Hermes (the Unbroken/endurance and synthesis), and Anansi (the Spark/morale and agitation).
rules.source: Character Codex, Ezio Valcari — The Revolutionary Trio

rules.statement: Lauris Letitia is a Karesian (Kares Prime) warrior serving as Ezio Valcari's Attia (Sergeant-at-Arms); she is a former top-tier Sealbound Directorate external contractor who defected after discovering the Directorate's structural ignorance of its own legacy systems.
rules.source: Character Codex, Lauris Letitia — Identity / SBD History

rules.statement: Lauris's signature weapon, Attia's Rite (a leaf-shaped breaker), was forged by Kanja Rexmar as a gift to Ezio for his Sergeant-at-Arms.
rules.source: Character Codex, Lauris Letitia — The Attia / Arsenal

rules.statement: Hermes' true name is Fermand Aurelias; he is a pure human (no exotic biology) and a former high-ranking intelligence officer of a Free State, captured and tortured for years at the Black Iron Citadel before escaping.
rules.source: Character Codex, Hermes — Identity / Origin

rules.statement: Fermand (Hermes) narrates all Ezio and Lauris POV chapters in a Baroque/Zafón-Noir voice, distinct from Onyx's narration of Kanja.
rules.source: Character Codex, Hermes — Narrative Voice

rules.statement: Valen's true name is Valen; his ship title is Sinisterblade, SBD designation SBD-008, and his biology is the 'Precision Variant' with lower static density than heavyweights but shatter-proof durability exceeding Branded Peak (2,200x–4,900x).
rules.source: Character Codex, Valen — Identity

rules.statement: Valen is identified as T.D.K.'s single worst-case Warbody opponent because his gap-finding, nerve-strike combat style turns the Warbody's structural interfaces into liabilities.
rules.source: Character Codex, Valen — Warbody Matchup / Canon Mandates
rules.note: Consistent with Anu Un Ra's own Warbody matchup table, which separately confirms Valen as the WORST-CASE matchup.

rules.statement: Sephtis's true name is Vrail; he is 1,997 years old, SBD designation SBD-003, and is the Lords of Cian's lead tactician/logistician.
rules.source: Character Codex, Sephtis — Identity

rules.statement: Sephtis personally knew the Kareth War-Order and both Kareth sisters (Val Saeryn and Val Mirel) — the mothers of Kanja and Ozmund respectively.
rules.source: Character Codex, Sephtis — Role & Philosophy / Key Relationships

rules.statement: Sephtis does not know that Archon Meridian is secretly Archon Un Ra, T.D.K.'s hidden son; he privately regards Archon as merely 'a Tenant in Default.'
rules.source: Character Codex, Sephtis — Key Relationships / Canon Mandates
rules.note: Consistent with the locked fact that Archon Meridian is secretly T.D.K.'s hidden son and does not know it himself; this adds that Sephtis also does not know.

rules.statement: Bloodreaver's true name is Torian; his Cruor-Kin biology runs blood at near-boiling temperature, and per an explicit in-document canon rule, all of his combat effects are physical/thermodynamic only — he has no Tongue (frequency-craft) application.
rules.source: Character Codex, Bloodreaver — Identity / Canon Rule (explicit in-document canon rule)

rules.statement: Ironbane's true name is Darius, SBD designation SBD-005; his bio-electric powers require the Ionic Ground bracer as life support — removing or damaging it causes fatal self-incineration (Critical Overload).
rules.source: Character Codex, Ironbane — Identity / Weaknesses

rules.statement: Anansi's true name is Anansi; his SBD/enemy designation 'Shadowforge' is an explicit in-document canon correction stating these are the SAME person, not two separate identities.
rules.source: Character Codex, Anansi — Identity (explicit 'CANON CORRECTION' statement)

rules.statement: Anansi is secretly the brother of Valeria Korth; this is classified and not known to Ozmund or the Sovereign Trust.
rules.source: Character Codex, Anansi — Key Relationships / Canon Mandates
rules.note: Confirms the locked fact that Anansi and Valeria Korth are secretly siblings.

rules.statement: Stormbreaker's true name is Kaelen; he is explicitly a separate Avatar from Stormreaver (Kairo) — the document notes them as distinct characters who are sometimes conflated.
rules.source: Character Codex, Stormbreaker — Canon Mandates; Stormreaver — Canon Note

rules.statement: Stormbreaker (Kaelen) is the one who fought and defeated the Demaron entity possessing Pyro's mother during the Living Gate event, with Kanja's consent, and also serves as Pyro's guardian without Pyro knowing this history. The Codex's own framing that this 'ended her body's vessel' is deliberate in-universe misdirection (per MCD-133); MCD-131/MCD-132 are the sole authorial truth -- she survived, inverting the Gate into a forge and fusing into its architecture rather than being ended.
rules.source: Character Codex, Stormbreaker — Key Relationships / Canon Mandates; Pyro — Origin
rules.note: RESOLVED per CONFLICT-005 and MCD-133 (2026-08-22): this 'killed' language is deliberate in-world misdirection by design, not a contradiction to fix. MCD-131/MCD-132 remain the objective truth that she survived, fused into the Living Gate.

rules.statement: The Living Gate event: T.D.K. (Anu Un Ra) installed a voice-keyed 'Living Gate' curse into Kanja's first and only wife (a veil-reader) as a containment response to her discovering his hidden architecture; her pregnancy amplified the Gate, a Demaron entity inhabited her, and Pyro and the three Dhar-Kael guardians (Varkul, Varruk, Sorya) were produced as her final act. The Codex's own framing that her 'body's vessel was ultimately ended' is deliberate in-universe misdirection (per MCD-133); MCD-131/MCD-132 are the sole authorial truth -- she survived, inverting the Gate into a forge and fusing into its architecture rather than being ended.
rules.source: Character Codex, Pyro — Origin (The Living Gate)
rules.note: Reinforces the locked fact that the Triad Guardians (Varkul, Varruk, Sorya) originated from the Living Gate event involving Pyro's mother. See CC-045/MCD-133: the 'her body's vessel was ultimately ended' language is deliberate in-world misdirection, not an unresolved conflict.

rules.statement: Pyro's hidden birth name is Ignis Rexmar; he is Kanja's biological son and does not know his own parentage.
rules.source: Character Codex, Pyro — Identity / Secrets

rules.statement: The three Dhar-Kael ('last of the Bound Ones' — Varkul, Varruk, Sorya) are permanently and non-transferably bonded to Pyro specifically, not to the ship or crew as a whole.
rules.source: Character Codex, Pyro — Identity / Triad Bond; Drown-Warden Varkul, Sorya, Varruk — Identity & Classification

rules.statement: Drown-Warden Varkul is designated TRIAD-1, homages the mythic figure Svadilfari, and can morph between a ~4,025 lb Land Form and an 88%-larger Hydro-Titan Form as a natural adaptive (not shapeshifting-power) response to submersion.
rules.source: Character Codex, Drown-Warden Varkul — Morphology / Canon Mandates

rules.statement: Sorya is designated TRIAD-3, homages Muninn (Memory), and physically senses the vibration of a broken vow (Vow-Taste) as her primary betrayal-detection ability.
rules.source: Character Codex, Sorya — Identity & Classification / Capabilities

rules.statement: Varruk is designated TRIAD-2, homages Huginn (Thought), and provides aerial reconnaissance and pattern reconstruction via an ability called Angle-Whisper.
rules.source: Character Codex, Varruk — Identity & Classification / Capabilities
rules.note: Note the name collision: Kanja's telepathic bone-conduction communication method with Onyx is also called 'Angle-Whisper' elsewhere in the codex — the document reuses the same term for two unrelated abilities belonging to different characters.

rules.statement: Anu Un Ra's true name is confirmed as Anu Un Ra, with the document explicitly noting this corrects a prior/alternate name 'Argul.'
rules.source: Character Codex, Anu Un Ra — Identity / Canon Mandates (explicit in-document correction)
rules.note: Confirms the locked fact that T.D.K.'s true name is Anu Un Ra.

rules.statement: Anu Un Ra is 30,000+ years old and, per an explicit in-document canon rule, uses no Tongue (frequency-craft) application — all his capabilities are physical, engineered, biological, procedural, or psychological.
rules.source: Character Codex, Anu Un Ra — Identity / Canon Rule (explicit in-document canon rule)

rules.statement: Anu Un Ra's hidden son is Archon Meridian (true identity Archon Un Ra), who leads the Meridian Compact and does not know his own parentage.
rules.source: Character Codex, Anu Un Ra — Identity / What He Built That Still Stands
rules.note: Confirms the locked fact that Archon Meridian is secretly T.D.K.'s hidden son who does not know it.

rules.statement: Anu Un Ra's Pi-Vulnerability is the only thing in 30,000 years that has ever forced him to retreat; he cannot touch a Pi-Awakened Rexmar directly and must rely on proxies.
rules.source: Character Codex, Anu Un Ra — The Pi-Vulnerability

rules.statement: Haku (Kanja's ancestor) is the only being who ever forced Anu Un Ra to retreat, roughly 5,000 years ago, deposing him from the Old Dominion; Anu Un Ra sees Kanja as 'Haku's echo.'
rules.source: Character Codex, Anu Un Ra — The Pi-Vulnerability / Canon Mandates

rules.statement: The Kingdoms of Merak were a civilization of individually ancient sovereign rulers (including a younger Anu Un Ra) that predates the Old Dominion by tens of thousands of years; Anu Un Ra dismantled nearly all of them over an estimated 30,000–40,000 years, and the 'Shattered Kingdoms' are named for this ancient purge, not the Old Dominion's collapse roughly 5,000 years ago.
rules.source: Character Codex, Orlok — III-B. What Orlok Knows: The Kingdoms of Merak

rules.statement: Orlok is approximately 76,003 years old, a self-taught S-Tier fighter who reaches 20,000x density (equal to Vargo Vakas's static ceiling) temporarily through cultivation rather than augmentation; he is younger only than T.D.K. (Anu Un Ra).
rules.source: Character Codex, Orlok — Identity / Age

rules.statement: Orlok's staff, the Zenith-Rod, was reforged by Kanja using Living Drakma sourced from Moonvault reserves, raising Orlok's Kinetic Ascension ceiling from 18,000x to 20,000x.
rules.source: Character Codex, Orlok — Arsenal: The Zenith-Rod

rules.statement: Voidbreaker's true name is Jax; his 'Spatial Variant' negative-density biology makes him effectively uncapturable by standard restraints.
rules.source: Character Codex, Voidbreaker — Identity / Abilities

rules.statement: Ghostwind's true name is Sylas; he has the lowest static density ('Hollowed Density') of any Avatar and serves as forward scout/atmospheric stealth specialist.
rules.source: Character Codex, Ghostwind — Identity / Physical Description & Biology

rules.statement: Stormreaver's true name is Kairo; his Aero Variant biology (hollow-core bones, Falcon-Pack wings) is explicitly noted as a separate character from Stormbreaker (Kaelen), whose siege-artillery role is unrelated.
rules.source: Character Codex, Stormreaver — Identity (explicit 'Canon Note')

rules.statement: Soulreaver Zora's true name is Zora; she is the ship's Bosun/Deck Disciplinarian with Atmospheric Variant (barometric/asphyxiation) biology, and is romantically paired with Ironbane.
rules.source: Character Codex, Soulreaver Zora — Identity / Key Relationships

rules.statement: Damu's true name is Julian Dael-Koss; his Cruor-Variant biology lets him read a person's complete physiological state through blood contact, and he was the first person to confirm Kanja's Pi-Awakening (by feeling the chemistry shift through the ship's hull).
rules.source: Character Codex, Damu — Identity / Capability

rules.statement: Damu (Julian) monitors the 99.9% energy drain of Kanja's Internal Quench and has tracked its progression for over a century, but has never told Kanja the full results.
rules.source: Character Codex, Damu — Relationships

rules.statement: Abyss's true name is Ren Oshaal; his Negative-Density biology generates a localized gravitational-pressure field (passive +30% within 5m, active +200% within 15m, or a maximum-output 'Depth-Charge' crush within 1m), and he carries no weapons — his body is the arsenal.
rules.source: Character Codex, Abyss — Identity / Capability / Arsenal

rules.statement: Matar has no surname and no known origin beyond having been brought to Kanja by Sephtis roughly 400 years ago; he is a Termination Specialist with standard (non-variant) biology operating at 800x through methodology and discipline rather than density.
rules.source: Character Codex, Matar — Identity / Origin

rules.statement: Cooper's true name is Ronan Kellsward; his Mass-Compression Variant biology lets him absorb external mass through contact to temporarily raise his density (200x resting up to ~4,500x loaded), and he serves as the crew's Quartermaster/logistics architect.
rules.source: Character Codex, Cooper — Identity / Capability

rules.statement: Valeria Korth's Thread-Perception biology lets her read structural/causal connections as visible threads; she has escaped three separate Sealbound Directorate containment attempts.
rules.source: Character Codex, Valeria Korth — Identity / Capability

rules.statement: Valeria Korth is Kanja's best friend, love interest, and emotional anchor; the document carries an explicit hard canon mandate that 'VALERIA MUST SURVIVE.'
rules.source: Character Codex, Valeria Korth — Identity / Canon Mandates (explicit in-document canon mandate)

rules.statement: Valeria Korth knows Ozmund carries T.D.K.'s Crown-Scar architecture (perceiving it as a 'thread' in her web) but has told Kanja rather than Ozmund, judging the secret 'not hers to cut.'
rules.source: Character Codex, Valeria Korth — Relationships

rules.statement: Lady Nadea Thren is an independent operator, explicitly NOT T.D.K.'s champion or under anyone's control, who defected from the SBD's Division of Perceptual Analytics after discovering the Founder's Blueprints proving the SBD's containment doctrine was built on T.D.K.'s Ionic Rite architecture.
rules.source: Character Codex, Lady Nadea Thren — Identity / The Defection

rules.statement: Lady Nadea Thren is Ezio Valcari's patron and is genuinely, secretly in love with him; Ezio figured out years ago that she is 'the Viper' and stays anyway.
rules.source: Character Codex, Lady Nadea Thren — The Ezio Dynamic

rules.statement: Lady Nadea Thren was Fermand's (Hermes') Case Officer during his Black Iron Citadel interrogation period and has read his unredacted file.
rules.source: Character Codex, Lady Nadea Thren — The Ezio Dynamic

rules.statement: The document's own internal count of Talisman-protected Avatars is inconsistent: Kanja's Talisman of Mao section states the Sovereign Umbrella (Stage 1) protects '16 Avatars,' while Sephtis's and Anansi's sections both reference '17 Avatars,' and Soulreaver Zora's Canon Mandates calls her the '17th crewmate.'
rules.source: Character Codex, Kanja Rexmar — 5-B Talisman System (Stage 1) vs Sephtis — Role & Philosophy; Anansi — Abilities; Soulreaver Zora — Canon Mandates
rules.note: Internal document inconsistency (16 vs 17), not a conflict with the outside ledger — flagging for the team's own continuity tracking.

rules.statement: The document declares itself complete at '─── END OF CHARACTER CODEX (26 entries) ───' immediately after Lady Nadea Thren's entry, then continues with nine additional entries (Damu, Abyss, Matar, Cooper, Valeria Korth, Orlok, and a second, contradictory Lilith Cyzak entry) that are themselves separately labeled 'entries #25–29' and 'Entry #30'/'#31' — numbering that overlaps with the entries already counted in the '26 entries' total.
rules.source: Character Codex, structural end-marker at Soulreaver Zora's close, and subsequent 'ENTRIES #25–29: THE FINAL FIVE' / 'Character Codex Entry #30' / 'CC Entry #31' headers
rules.note: Document self-contradicts its own completion marker and entry numbering — flagged in document_notes as well.

rules.statement: The opening pages of the document (before the first '# CHARACTER' header) begin mid-sentence describing Kanja's biology and contain a large duplicated block of text — the same set of battle summaries (Battles 11–22 and their section headers) appears twice in immediate succession.
rules.source: Character Codex, opening pages (Kanja Rexmar section, pre-header material)
rules.note: Likely a docx export/copy-paste artifact rather than intentional canon; flagged in document_notes.

rules.statement: The document's version label is 'v1.0 — Comprehensive Character Bible' on its title page, and a later section footer independently repeats 'The Lords of Cian | Character Codex v1.0,' but the filename supplied for this review is 'LORDS_OF_CIAN_Character_Codex_definitive.docx.'
rules.source: Character Codex, title page and Soulreaver Zora section-end footer
rules.note: Flagging the version-label vs filename mismatch ('v1.0' internally vs 'definitive' in the filename) for the team's tracking, per the pattern of prior version-stamp oddities found in other documents.

rules.statement: Kanja considers Pyro his son and is aware of this, but hides it from Pyro; multiple guardians (Stormbreaker, Azar/Dreadlord) also know or suspect the lineage while Pyro himself does not.
rules.source: Character Codex, Kanja Rexmar — Key Relationships; Pyro — Secrets

rules.statement: Bloodreaver (Torian) is described as the only crew member, besides Kanja himself, physically able to restrain Kanja without being crushed.
rules.source: Character Codex, Bloodreaver — Key Relationships

rules.statement: The Character Codex (CC-045/CC-046) and the SBD Directives (SBD-010) both state Pyro's mother died during the Living Gate event. This is deliberate misdirection built into the world's own documents, not a continuity error -- multiple in-universe records converge on the same false conclusion by design, so anyone consulting the Codex or SBD casework has every reason to believe she is dead. MCD-131 and MCD-132 remain the sole objective account of what actually happened to her: she survived, inverting the Living Gate into a forge rather than being sealed by it, fused into its architecture.
rules.source: Operator ruling, 2026-08-22, resolving CONFLICT-005 (approved verbatim: 'i need those sections to believe that she is dead. it is deliberately there for this purpose... SBD also has conflicting information. this is meant to be deliberate.')
rules.note: Extends the CONFLICT-002 pattern (SBD's own account already ruled unreliable institutional narrative, 2026-08-15) to the Character Codex as well -- both documents are now understood as in-world sources built to misdirect, not drafting errors needing correction. MCD-131/MCD-132 stand as the authorial truth beneath both.

rules.statement: Lilith Cyzak is a former Sovereign Trust scientist and economic analyst, brilliant enough at both to have walked away from the Trust on principle. She has no inherent physical power. Her durability comes from a transfusion treatment using Ozmund's blood -- dangerous at the outset, she nearly died from it more than once, before stabilizing at a threshold that permits further enhancement as the series progresses. Ozmund and Red Beard train her in combat; her skill climbs across the books until she is able to spar against both of them directly, not merely survive being near them. When circumstances call for it she is capable of economic terrorism, applied with a Robin-Hood ideology rather than pure destruction: targeted, redistributive, principled. She remains Ozmund's calibration point through cost-benefit reasoning and decodes Directorate communications (consistent with CC-024's 'Lilith is Ozmund's'). This is the sole canon profile for the character. The Character Codex's separate 'Void-Dancer' entry (a physical bodyguard/anchor for Ozmund with Ghost-Step Algorithm, Thread-Relay, and Base-Grout abilities, no economic background) is discarded, superseding CC-025's flagged internal conflict.
rules.source: Operator ruling, 2026-08-22, resolving CC-025
rules.note: Resolves the Character Codex's internal Lilith Cyzak conflict flagged in CC-025. The economic-analyst entry (Codex #31) is the seed this rule builds from and expands well past; the Void-Dancer entry is not canon in any form.

rules.statement: Anu Un Ra's naming: True Name Anu Un Ra. Common Title (historical) The Deposed King. Earliest Recorded Title The Ash-King, from the Broken Meridian era. Functional Title Architect of the Ionic Rite.
rules.source: DOSSIER: ANU UN RA (Lore Vault)
rules.note: Originally drafted from 'World Codex v3.4' (WC- rules) or the Lore Vault's 'DOSSIER: ANU UN RA' (CULT- rules) early in the project, before the explicit draft-then-approval workflow was formalized. Cross-checked against the full live ledger (719 rules, 44 batches) in Batch 45 and found consistent with everything since locked; several independently corroborate later-locked material (e.g. WC-018's Five Champions roster and WC-020's Deposition account both match the now-locked CULT-family Anu Un Ra rules exactly). Promoted to locked per Abad's blanket authorization: "you have my authorization to reconcile".

rules.statement: Anu Un Ra's governing doctrine runs on five principles: continuity over victory (short-term loss is acceptable if it preserves long-term control infrastructure), systems over combat (direct fighting is inefficient and increases exposure), a containment-first worldview (hazards are resources once captured and made predictable), information dominance (records, identities, and registries are controllable assets), and institutional parasitism (he allows others to inherit, maintain, and expand his frameworks, then reasserts root control when required).
rules.source: DOSSIER: ANU UN RA (Lore Vault)
rules.note: Originally drafted from 'World Codex v3.4' (WC- rules) or the Lore Vault's 'DOSSIER: ANU UN RA' (CULT- rules) early in the project, before the explicit draft-then-approval workflow was formalized. Cross-checked against the full live ledger (719 rules, 44 batches) in Batch 45 and found consistent with everything since locked; several independently corroborate later-locked material (e.g. WC-018's Five Champions roster and WC-020's Deposition account both match the now-locked CULT-family Anu Un Ra rules exactly). Promoted to locked per Abad's blanket authorization: "you have my authorization to reconcile".

rules.statement: Anu Un Ra is controlled, clinical, and contemptuous toward opponents, motivated by permanent control of outcomes and elimination of succession instability. He avoids personal combat, regarding it as work for subordinates and assets, and is highly risk-averse about structural exposure, willing to sacrifice territory, reputation, and personnel to protect his core systems.
rules.source: DOSSIER: ANU UN RA (Lore Vault)
rules.note: Promoted from draft to locked in Batch 44, independently corroborated by the Anu Un Ra Psychological Profile document.

rules.statement: Before the Old Dominion, Anu ruled Broken Meridian, a subterranean pre-imperial state. Deep excavation there uncovered the Meridian Engine, a sealed prehuman constraint-modeling device producing scenario projections, resource dependency mapping, and failure-mode exposure through light, vibration, and heat-gradient outputs. He linked his own biology to it under an exchange protocol, causing irreversible physiological degradation and permanent dependence on maintenance cycles, then staged his own public death and transitioned into long-term controlled storage with intermittent reactivation. This period founds the Order of the Ionic Rite.
rules.source: DOSSIER: ANU UN RA (Lore Vault)
rules.note: Promoted from draft to locked in Batch 44, independently corroborated by the Anu Un Ra Psychological Profile document, which also supplies the Warbody-as-life-support framing at CULT-194.

rules.statement: The Order of the Ionic Rite is Anu Un Ra's original operating tradition for anomaly study and containment, running a fixed methodology: study, pursue, capture, contain, document. Its tools are engineered traps, layered physical containment, environmental control, psychophysiological conditioning through controlled stimuli, and standardized documentation. Its purpose is converting uncontrollable hazards into predictable assets; its legacy is that later institutions inherit Ionic Rite sites and standards without understanding the dependencies embedded in them.
rules.source: DOSSIER: ANU UN RA (Lore Vault)
rules.note: Promoted from draft to locked in Batch 44, independently corroborated by the Anu Un Ra Psychological Profile document.

rules.statement: The Old Dominion was built around death logistics and containment discipline: physical death-tech (preservation, reanimation, neural residue mapping, bioelectric harvesting), bureaucratic control of death, records, and labor, and a posture where every conflict yields materials, bodies, intelligence, and leverage.
rules.source: DOSSIER: ANU UN RA (Lore Vault)
rules.note: Originally drafted from 'World Codex v3.4' (WC- rules) or the Lore Vault's 'DOSSIER: ANU UN RA' (CULT- rules) early in the project, before the explicit draft-then-approval workflow was formalized. Cross-checked against the full live ledger (719 rules, 44 batches) in Batch 45 and found consistent with everything since locked; several independently corroborate later-locked material (e.g. WC-018's Five Champions roster and WC-020's Deposition account both match the now-locked CULT-family Anu Un Ra rules exactly). Promoted to locked per Abad's blanket authorization: "you have my authorization to reconcile".

rules.statement: Anu Un Ra's fall is recorded as a defeat but functioned as a strategic withdrawal. The real causes were Haku's multi-front overstretch campaign and internal betrayal by his second-in-command, Verehimu. Rather than risk total structural exposure, he let the Old Dominion collapse as a visible political entity while preserving core infrastructure and relocating.
rules.source: DOSSIER: ANU UN RA (Lore Vault)
rules.note: Originally drafted from 'World Codex v3.4' (WC- rules) or the Lore Vault's 'DOSSIER: ANU UN RA' (CULT- rules) early in the project, before the explicit draft-then-approval workflow was formalized. rules.statement: The Sealbound Directorate is a later institution built on inherited Ionic Rite foundations, believing itself a neutral containment authority. In reality its oldest sites are retrofitted Ionic Rite vaults, and its core standards carry legacy assumptions and physical backdoors: legacy lock sequences, maintenance-keyed stability requirements, and root protocol hierarchies embedded in the earliest architecture. Anu Un Ra's strategy is to let the SBD co-opt and expand his infrastructure without his own exposure, then reassert control selectively.
rules.source: DOSSIER: ANU UN RA (Lore Vault)
rules.note: Originally drafted from 'World Codex v3.4' (WC- rules) or the Lore Vault's 'DOSSIER: ANU UN RA' (CULT- rules) early in the project, before the explicit draft-then-approval workflow was formalized. rules.statement: Under Anu Un Ra's control: the Ever-Haunt, originless pursuit entities captured and conditioned in the Shattered Kingdoms, used as personal hounds and the core of his Hunt division (maps to the existing Division 2, Echoes/Nameless Pursuit, under Sereth Vaul). Selected perception anomalies used for deception and misdirection (maps to Division 3, Mirages/Illusions, under Lady Vestige). Select cataclysm-tier organisms used for siege leverage and territory denial (maps to Division 4, Crownless Host/Dominion, under Lord Varro Dominael). His Book 1 epilogue return activates legacy dependencies in the SBD's oldest infrastructure as a targeted, selective breach, not a total collapse, reclaiming the Ever-Haunt and select anomalies and signaling the shift from dormancy to active execution.
rules.source: DOSSIER: ANU UN RA (Lore Vault)
rules.note: Originally drafted from 'World Codex v3.4' (WC- rules) or the Lore Vault's 'DOSSIER: ANU UN RA' (CULT- rules) early in the project, before the explicit draft-then-approval workflow was formalized. Cross-checked against the full live ledger (719 rules, 44 batches) in Batch 45 and found consistent with everything since locked; several independently corroborate later-locked material (e.g. WC-018's Five Champions roster and WC-020's Deposition account both match the now-locked CULT-family Anu Un Ra rules exactly). Promoted to locked per Abad's blanket authorization: "you have my authorization to reconcile".

rules.statement: Of the five divisions locked in MCD-050, three map cleanly to named asset categories in the Anu Un Ra dossier: Division 2 to Ever-Haunt Hunt operations, Division 3 to perception/illusion assets, Division 4 to siege-leverage organisms. Division 1 (Weights/Conquest, open warfare under Baryon) remains conventional military. Division 5, under Bolo Troth, is his institutional-subversion and cult-coordination command -- the dossier's own account of his primary control toolkit (institutional manipulation, kompromat, procedural warfare, records and identity sabotage) fits no other division's combat/containment character. This is the division responsible for running the Legion-corruption cult network.
rules.source: Operator ruling, 2026-08-22, resolving OPEN-004 (approved verbatim: 'THE BATCH READS RIGHT. WE WILL GO WITH THE RECOMENDATIONS')
rules.note: Resolves OPEN-004.

rules.statement: The Weighing Communities' founding claim is geographic, not genealogical. They believe T.D.K. placed Anchor Stones as territorial markers during the Kingdoms of Merak purges and that residual frequency from the stones accumulates in bodies that live near them across generations. The stones are real and were placed by T.D.K., but have been inert for 30,000 to 40,000 years. The communities' actual above-average density comes from Merak-purge survival selection: high-density individuals survived the purges at higher rates, settled near the boundary markers, and five thousand years of the community's own measurement-and-preference culture applied generational selection pressure in the direction they believed the stones were causing. The belief in the mechanism is wrong. The outcome the belief describes is real.
rules.source: Cult Dossier file 'Weighing Communities' (Google Drive fileId 1F301LbnBlDOajOvmOuHbT_zheWrwlbKi), Batch 12, approved by Abad 2026-08-22

rules.statement: Roughly forty Weighing Communities occupy the administrative borderland between the Hollow Shogunate and the Astral Archipelago's outer island chain, a margin no government has ever fully claimed. Authority runs Weigher (highest-density adult, verified by a standardized stone-weight system shared across communities through periodic exchange) over Scale-Keepers (Ledger-keepers, one or two per community) over Bearers (working members) over the Uncounted (identified but unmeasured candidates). Succession is non-elective: whoever measures highest at a Weigher's death or incapacitation inherits the role regardless of age or experience.
rules.source: Cult Dossier file 'Weighing Communities' (Google Drive fileId 1F301LbnBlDOajOvmOuHbT_zheWrwlbKi), Batch 12, approved by Abad 2026-08-22

rules.statement: The core Weighing Communities observance is a weekly stone-platform measurement recorded into a lifetime density trajectory. The measurement is a pressure/mass proxy, not a true density reading, and is skewed by diet, hydration, and health. Experienced Scale-Keepers apply an unrecorded oral tradition of contextual adjustment that, in practice, makes the system a sophisticated (if undocumented) community health-monitoring practice. Communities that have lost this oral tradition take raw numbers at face value.
rules.source: Cult Dossier file 'Weighing Communities' (Google Drive fileId 1F301LbnBlDOajOvmOuHbT_zheWrwlbKi), Batch 12, approved by Abad 2026-08-22

rules.statement: The Weighing Communities' second observance, the Frequency Submission, is a monthly new-moon group vocalization ('the Tonal Register') performed at the community's Anchor Stone. The verse is an accurate but non-functional fragment of an actual Ten Tongues frequency pattern. It produces a real, measurable bioelectric-coherence effect, generated by the resonance of the gathered bodies interacting with the stone's mineral composition, which the communities misattribute to the King's attention rather than to themselves.
rules.source: Cult Dossier file 'Weighing Communities' (Google Drive fileId 1F301LbnBlDOajOvmOuHbT_zheWrwlbKi), Batch 12, approved by Abad 2026-08-22

rules.statement: The Weighing Communities are actively hunting two relic categories: a seventh, unlocated primary Anchor Stone (its location is known only to the Measurist Guild's Master Surveyor, who withholds it as personal negotiating leverage), and Old Dominion calibration rods, which they buy from brokers at good rates without asking about provenance.
rules.source: Cult Dossier file 'Weighing Communities' (Google Drive fileId 1F301LbnBlDOajOvmOuHbT_zheWrwlbKi), Batch 12, approved by Abad 2026-08-22

rules.statement: For approximately sixty years, Weighing Community runners have served as the Concordat of the Long Account's courier network through the Shogunate-Archipelago borderland, paid in Scrip that the communities fold into their own relic-acquisition fund. The runners inspect nothing they carry and do not know they are funding, and competing with, their own object hunt.
rules.source: Cult Dossier file 'Weighing Communities' (Google Drive fileId 1F301LbnBlDOajOvmOuHbT_zheWrwlbKi), Batch 12, approved by Abad 2026-08-22

rules.statement: Post-Great Breach, the Weighing Communities have tripled their measurement frequency, which has broken the informal Scale-Keeper adjustment tradition in communities that can't sustain it at that volume. This is producing false 'Hollow' (structurally-unsafe, socially excluded) designations against healthy members. Several families have responded by self-exiling into the borderland, maintaining private Accounting outside community structure, rather than abandoning the practice outright.
rules.source: Cult Dossier file 'Weighing Communities' (Google Drive fileId 1F301LbnBlDOajOvmOuHbT_zheWrwlbKi), Batch 12, approved by Abad 2026-08-22

rules.statement: Fourteen of the roughly forty Weighing Communities now sit inside territory the crew holds or contests after the Great Breach. This places a live, sixty-year-old Concordat courier infrastructure inside the crew's own territory, unknown to the crew and not understood by the communities running it, who have never known what they carry.
rules.source: Cult Dossier file 'Weighing Communities' (Google Drive fileId 1F301LbnBlDOajOvmOuHbT_zheWrwlbKi), Batch 12, approved by Abad 2026-08-22

rules.statement: The Ledger Families claim descent from T.D.K.'s court scribes and hold a 'Family Ledger,' a 5,000-year chain-of-custody transcription that is approximately forty percent accurate to the lost original. The inaccuracy is not evenly distributed: the most heavily copied, most operationally significant passages (governance procedure, frequency architecture, Crown-Scar installation) are the most corrupted, because they were copied most often, by the widest range of scribes, under the most pressure to stay readable.
rules.source: Cult Dossier file 'Weighing Communities' (Google Drive fileId 1F301LbnBlDOajOvmOuHbT_zheWrwlbKi), Batch 12, approved by Abad 2026-08-22

rules.statement: Forty-three families are currently recognized Ledger Family network members, authenticated by reciting matched Ledger passages against a family's own copy at a seventy-percent textual-agreement threshold; four families sit in provisional status, two of them for over a generation, because their copies have diverged too far to reconcile.
rules.source: Cult Dossier file 'Weighing Communities' (Google Drive fileId 1F301LbnBlDOajOvmOuHbT_zheWrwlbKi), Batch 12, approved by Abad 2026-08-22

rules.statement: Every seven years, Ledger Family heads elect a senior Accountant who adjudicates textual disputes and recognizes new families. Daily Accounting is a synchronized reading, one Ledger passage per day on an eleven-year rotation, performed at the same hour by every family across all five Shattered Kingdoms nations. Missing a reading without cause accrues a compliance deficit; past a threshold, voting rights are suspended until cleared. The synchronization is, functionally, a distributed communications network the families built without meaning to.
rules.source: Cult Dossier file 'Weighing Communities' (Google Drive fileId 1F301LbnBlDOajOvmOuHbT_zheWrwlbKi), Batch 12, approved by Abad 2026-08-22

rules.statement: The Ledger Families have run a funded, three-hundred-year archaeological excavation in the Kingdoms of Merak ruins, seeking the lost original document. Eight months before Book One, they found a sealed chamber matching an Old Dominion archive profile and have not opened it. Three parties currently know the chamber's location by three separate routes (the Measurist Guild via True Map annotation, the Concordat via the Guild's intelligence-sharing arrangement, the families via their own dig), and none has told the others.
rules.source: Cult Dossier file 'Weighing Communities' (Google Drive fileId 1F301LbnBlDOajOvmOuHbT_zheWrwlbKi), Batch 12, approved by Abad 2026-08-22

rules.statement: The Ledger Families' Ledger-authentication expertise has made them a paid authentication authority for Old Dominion documents across the cult ecosystem, including material they were never meant to see. A senior Ledger Family head has personally handled a rubbing of the Domus Inviolate's Crown-Scar documentation (via a broker transaction; see CULT-030's Concordat cross-reference), giving her unrecognized interpretive context for a previously opaque Ledger passage that Fermand will be able to read within hours of encountering both.
rules.source: Cult Dossier file 'Weighing Communities' (Google Drive fileId 1F301LbnBlDOajOvmOuHbT_zheWrwlbKi), Batch 12, approved by Abad 2026-08-22

rules.statement: Post-Great Breach, the Ledger Families are reading their most heavily edited passage (the Resumption sequence) and finding that several listed preconditions have already occurred, convincing a majority that the Resumption is underway and the sealed chamber must be opened immediately rather than after normal deliberation. The family council is split between this urgency faction and a cautious faction wary of exposing the operation.
